title: React TypeScript Core Check
description: Check your understanding of TypeScript with React props, state, hooks, events, generics, context, discriminated unions, and common typing mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a main benefit of typing component props?

options.text: It documents and enforces the component contract at compile time

questions.explanation: Prop types describe what a component expects, helping catch incorrect usage before runtime.

questions.prompt: Which type is commonly used for renderable children in React TypeScript?
questions.explanation: React.ReactNode covers strings, numbers, elements, fragments, null, and other values React can render.

questions.prompt: How would you type a text input change handler parameter?
questions.explanation: Input change events use React.ChangeEvent with the relevant element type, such as HTMLInputElement.

questions.prompt: TypeScript validates API responses at runtime automatically.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is erased at runtime. External data still needs runtime validation when its shape cannot be trusted.

questions.prompt: When is an explicit generic useful with `useState`?

options.text: When initial state like `null` or `[]` does not give enough information
Only when the component has no props

questions.explanation: Examples like `useState<User | null>(null)` or `useState<Item[]>([])` give TypeScript the intended state shape.

questions.prompt: What is a discriminated union useful for in React props?

options.text: Modeling variants where allowed fields depend on a shared discriminant such as `kind` or `type`

questions.explanation: A discriminant field lets TypeScript narrow the correct prop shape for each variant.

questions.prompt: Which React areas commonly benefit from TypeScript? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Types are useful across component boundaries, state transitions, event handlers, and shared context contracts.

questions.prompt: Why wrap a nullable context in a custom hook?

options.text: To throw a clear error when the provider is missing and return a non-null value after the check
To make context update outside React

questions.explanation: A custom hook can centralize the provider check so consumers get a safer non-null value.
